name: Aringa
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Boone & Watson 1999 Moru-Ma'di Survey Report named (SIL page 403); a wordlist/intelligibility survey, no stress description located.

sources.citation: Kilpatrick, Eileen. 2004. Orthographies of Moru-Ma'di languages. Occasional Papers in the Study of Sudanese Languages 9: 85-91. Entebbe: SIL-Sudan.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Covers Aringa by name (p. 85) with segment inventory/grapheme charts and a 'Tones' section (p. 88): all Moru-Ma'di languages have three level tones H/M/L; 'Madi and Aringa also use tone to mark singular and plural distinctions'. No occurrence of stress/accent in the prosodic sense.

sources.citation: Boone, Douglas W. & Richard L. Watson (eds.). 1999. Moru-Ma'di survey report. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 1999-001. 260 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing (0 prosodic hits for stress/accent in 260 pp). Aringa = northernmost, most divergent Lugbara dialect ('Low Lugbara'); 'On the phonetic level, Aringa and Terego are closer than one would guess from the lexical data'; Appendix 8 notes Tucker's 1940 Lugbara data 'both lexically and phonetically most resembles the Aringa dialect'. Tone marked on wordlists only.
